memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Joseph said to his brothers, 'I am Joseph! Is my father still living?' But his brothers were not able to answer him, because they were terrified at his presence." — Gen 45:3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Three words change everything. "I am Joseph."

Imagine standing in that room. The powerful Egyptian in front of you, the man who holds your life in his hand, suddenly speaks your language — and tells you he is the brother you sold. Every calculation collapses. Every hope of escape vanishes. The brothers cannot say a single word. Scripture says they were terrified.

And yet look at what Joseph asks next. Not "how could you?" Not "do you remember what you did?" He asks, "Is my father still living?" His first thought is love, not revenge.

There is something here about how we meet Christ. The first time we truly see who Jesus is, it is often frightening. Peter fell at His knees and said, "Go away from me, Lord; I am a sinful man" (Lk 5:8). To stand before the One we have wronged, fully known and fully exposed, is a terrifying thing.

But the fear does not last, because of who He is. The One we sinned against is the One who came to save us. Christ does not reveal Himself to us in order to condemn us (Jn 3:17). He reveals Himself in order to bring us home.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you think of God's full knowledge of you as terrifying or as safe?
2. What was your first real awareness of who Jesus is?
3. Is there guilt keeping you at a distance from Him today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You know everything about me, including the worst of me, and You still call me to Yourself. Take away my fear and let me come close. Amen.
